AI Networking: Beyond Crazy
Alicia Xia Jeff Pu, CFA Evan Lee

What's new
We update that the total demand for 800G/1.6T will reach 43mn/30mn in 2026 (vs previous 37mn/28mn), mainly driven by: 1) Nvidia, Google and AWS’s accelerators’ demand; 2) GPU/ASIC scale-out bandwidth increase driving increasing number of GPU/ASIC-tooptical module ratio; 3) Google’s transitions to large-scale clusters in 2026 and the scale-up layer will likely adopt optical interconnects.
Comments
Raise 1.6T to 30m in 2026: We updated that the total shipment of 1.6T to 30mn in 2026, mainly driven by Nvidia’s Rubin, Rubin’s higher GPU-to-optical module ratio (from 1:2.5 to 1:5 1.6T) and demand for Google’s TPU which is better than expected. According to our report of AI: Reality Checks on CoWoS and ASICs on Oct 17, we now expect 377k/630k CoWoS for Nvidia in 2025/2026, from earlier 377k/580k, and this includes 50k for Vera CPUs, driven by the earlier ramp of Rubin which is scheduled for a mid-2026 package out thus, we expect 5m/2m Blackwell/Rubin in 2026, from CoWoS build perspective. Per our AI: 2026 CoWoS for TPU Better than Expected report, we estimate that AVGO’s cowos for 2026 will be 200k (vs 180k earlier), driven by robust TPU demand. We expect TPU shipments to be 2.7mn/4mn in 2025 and 2026 for now. Other than Apple, Meta, HPE, Oracle, Bytedance, Anthropic also announced 1m demand for TPU on Oct 24. As a result, we expect that CoWoS for Google may revise up to 220-230k and Google’s 1.6T has potential to revise up accordingly.
The increase of scale-out bandwidth driving the increase in optical-module deployment. For NVIDIA, each Rubin GPU is equipped with two CX9 NIC chips, doubling the scale-out bandwidth compared with Blackwell. We further estimate that Rubin Ultra will adopt four CX9 chips per GPU, leading to another 2 times increase in scale-out bandwidth, continuing NVIDIA’s consistent bandwidthdoubling trajectory. Accordingly, we expect the ratio of 1.6T optical modules has risen from 1:2.5 to 1:5 in Rubin. From CoWoS perspective, we expect 5m/2m Blackwell/Rubin and 20m 1.6T in 2026. For Google, we believe that Google fully transition to largescale clusters in 2026 and the scale-up layer will adopt optical interconnects. We believe that in the scale-up domain, the ratio of TPU to 1.6T optical modules is approximately 1:1.5; In the scale-out domain, the ratio is around 1:2.5, suggesting the overall TPU-to-optics ratio is approximately 1:4 (1.6T equivalent). We expect the 4m TPU will lead to 6m/10m 800G/1.6T for Google in 2026. For Meta, we believe that The Minera architecture features one ASIC chip paired with two NICs. The ASIC to optical module ratio is also driven by scale out bandwidth increase.
Key beneficiaries: We expect that the upward revision of the 1.6T is favorable for silicon photonics players like TSEM (Tower Semi), considering the shortage of EML, and switch/switch chip players like AVGO/CLS. We also like LITE, supported by rising EML demand and expected price increases in 2026. In addition, within its OCS switch business, we expect the total shipment of OCS will be 15k/30k in 2025/2026 and Lite will take 30% share in 2026. We believe that LITE is well positioned in the transition of optical communications toward scale-up architectures as well as in the evolution of scale-out upgrades, making it a strategically advantaged player.
CPO/OIO updates: According to our OCP report, Nvidia’s keynote at OCP demonstrate that MSFT’s Azure and Oracle’s Cloud will start to use Spectrum X. While we believe that CPO penetration rate is not meaningful in 1.6T generation, considering factors such as maturity, technical reliability, and the degree of decoupling. Meta mentioned that TH6 Bailly will not see significant volume. We maintain our estimation that Nvidia’s CPO switch will be 2k/20k/35k in 2025/2026/2027. As for OIO, we believe that starting from 2027, both NVIDIA and ASIC players are expected to have OIO related solutions, driving incremental demand for CW laser/FAU and optical engines. We believe the key beneficiaries will include Lite/FN and Chinese leading optical module players.
